text:
lee: Heads-up — nightly perf regression on fused-attn + TP for long sequences (seq=4096). Seeing ~12% slowdown compared to last week when running with flash-attn enabled. Looks tied to QKV all-gather fallback pattern and uneven device strides.

anya: ugh. can you paste the perf numbers and repro command? also which kernel picker flags were used?

lee: repro command:
```
./run_microbench --model gptx --seq 4096 --tp 2 --pp 1 --flash true --kernel-picker auto --batch 1
```
perf summary (median tokens/sec):
- baseline (no flash): 7800
- flash-attn w/ TP (current): 6880  <-- slow
- flash-attn w/o TP (single-gpu): 7900

observations:
- QKV all-gather happens more often with our TP sharding when seq > 2048 (we fall back to scatter+gather path due to alignment mismatch)
- kv-cache evictions spike (small bursts) correlated with the slowdown
- device 1 shows higher compute idle time during all-gather windows

david: can you share nvprof / per-kernel timings? curious if all-reduce latency or kernel selection is the culprit. also which cudnn/cutlass versions?

lee: nvprof snippet pasted below (trimmed):
```
[GPU0] flash_attn_kernel  4.1ms
[GPU1] all_gather_qkv     12.6ms <-- hotspot
[GPU0] compute             3.9ms
[GPU1] compute             2.9ms
```
cutlass: 2.7, cuda: 12.1

perf-bot: CI alert: nightly/fused-attn-tp regression at 1855000000 (detect_regression)

infra-bot: topology: 2xA100 NVLink ring, PCIe fallback observed between GPU1<->GPU0 during large AllGather windows.

anya: sounds like a comm/compute overlap failure. if GPU1 is blocked on AllGather and others finish compute earlier we lose overlap. possible causes: stride imbalance from TP sharding or batching heuristic that creates tiny micro-batches on some ranks.

sam: i pushed a tiny probe (wip) to try enforced symmetric QKV padding so we avoid fallback scatter/gather for odd tile sizes. want lee to run it. patch: --force-qkv-align=256

lee: ran with --force-qkv-align=256 -> tokens/sec improved to 7320 (partial recovery). nvprof shows all_gather_qkv -> 7.8ms now and compute idle reduced. no kv-cache evictions observed in short run.

david: nice. that indicates the kernel selection heuristics are choosing a non-flash path because of unaligned QKV shapes. two follow-ups:
- kernel-picker should try a padded-flash path when comm cost < threshold (i.e., trade small compute overhead for lower comm).
- batching heuristics: when tp>1 and seq large, prefer larger micro-batch grouping to amortize all-gather.

anya: Agreed. add a regression test in microbench that exercises seq in [1024,2048,4096,8192] with tp variants and requires <5% regression vs single-gpu flash baseline.

lee: noted. i'll run the full sweep overnight and attach flamegraphs. link: http://ci.internal/reports/1855000000/trace (private)

perf-bot: scheduled nightly sweep: fused-attn-tp-stride-sweep (seqs:1024,2048,4096,8192) — logs will be uploaded to the trace link above.

sam: also worth checking KV cache sharding: if we shard by head and not by position, we might trigger extra synchronization on cache hits. try fallback config: --kv-shard=pos for the sweep.

lee: plan for next steps:
1) run full seq sweep with --force-qkv-align and --kv-shard=pos (overnight)
2) add kernel-picker heuristic to prefer padded-flash when estimated all-gather > 6ms
3) add microbench regression tests and a perf alert to catch >8% regression on fused-attn+TP
4) if improvement still <90% of baseline, profile deeper for NVLink contention and consider async all-gather staggering.

anya: thanks — please update thread when sweep finishes. tagging @david @sam for visibility. :thumbsup:

lee: will do, thanks everyone.
